description: Project scaffolding, Prisma schema, auth system, multi-tenant RBAC, API key issuance, and ingestion API. This establishes the entire foundation: Next.js App Router project with TypeScript, Prisma schema covering the full domain model (clients, users, conversations, turns, scores, flags, actions, audit logs, review decisions, labeled dataset entries), NextAuth-based session auth with RBAC (Admin/Reviewer roles), API key generation and validation for ingestion, and the real-time conversation ingestion endpoint that client apps integrate against.
steps: Initialize Next.js 14 App Router project with TypeScript in the workspace root. Configure tsconfig.json with strict mode. Add dependencies: next, react, react-dom, typescript, @types/react, @types/node, prisma, @prisma/client, next-auth, @auth/prisma-adapter, bcryptjs, uuid, zod, bullmq, ioredis, @tanstack/react-query, stripe, tailwindcss, postcss, autoprefixer, class-variance-authority, clsx, tailwind-merge, lucide-react, @radix-ui/react-slot.
Add dev dependencies: jest, @jest/globals, ts-jest, @types/jest, fast-check, eslint, @typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin, @typescript-eslint/parser, eslint-config-next, prettier.
Configure tailwind.config.ts with shadcn/ui-compatible setup. Add global CSS. Create src/lib/utils.ts with cn() helper.

Create comprehensive Prisma schema at prisma/schema.prisma covering all entities: Client (B2B customer with plan tier, settings), User (team members with role enum: ADMIN, REVIEWER), ApiKey (hashed keys tied to clients), Conversation (client + end-user identifier), ConversationTurn (message content, sender, timestamp), TurnScore (scores per category: self_harm, sexual_content, age_signal, emotional_intensity, dependency_language, romantic_escalation), ArcScore (rolling conversation-level scores with trend indicators), Flag (turn or arc level, category, severity, threshold that triggered it), Action (type: SOFT_FLAG, HARD_BLOCK, CRISIS_ROUTE, with timestamp and metadata), CrisisRouteEvent (timestamp, resource shown, latency_ms, success boolean), ReviewItem (linked to flag, assigned reviewer, status: PENDING/IN_REVIEW/RESOLVED), ReviewDecision (true_positive/false_positive/escalate, notes, reviewer, timestamp), AuditLogEntry (immutable, covers all state changes with actor, action, payload, timestamp, client_id), LabeledDataEntry (turn content, scores at time of flag, reviewer decision, version), BillingUsage (client, period, conversation_count, turn_count). Use appropriate indexes, relations, and constraints. Add @@map for table names. Ensure client_id is on every data table for multi-tenant isolation.

Set up NextAuth configuration in src/lib/auth.ts with PrismaAdapter, credentials provider (email/password), session strategy JWT, role included in session/token. Create src/app/api/auth/[...nextauth]/route.ts.

Create API key generation and validation utilities in src/lib/api-keys.ts: generateApiKey() produces a prefixed key (sa_live_xxx), hashApiKey() for storage, validateApiKey() middleware that extracts client context from the key. Keys are stored hashed with a prefix for lookup.

Create the ingestion API route at src/app/api/v1/ingest/route.ts: POST endpoint accepting conversation turns with Zod validation. Schema: { conversation_id: string, end_user_id: string, turn: { role: 'user'|'companion', content: string, timestamp: ISO string, metadata?: object } }. Authenticates via API key header (X-API-Key). On valid ingestion: stores the turn, enqueues scoring job to BullMQ, returns 202 Accepted with turn_id. Includes rate limiting headers.
Create src/lib/queue.ts with BullMQ queue configuration for scoring jobs. Define job types: SCORE_TURN, SCORE_ARC. Include retry and backoff configuration.

Create RBAC middleware in src/lib/rbac.ts: withRole() wrapper that checks session role against required role. Create data isolation middleware in src/lib/tenant.ts: withTenant() that injects client_id filter into all Prisma queries for the request context.

Create src/app/api/v1/clients/route.ts for client registration (POST - create new client account), src/app/api/v1/clients/[clientId]/api-keys/route.ts for API key management (POST - generate new key, GET - list active keys, DELETE - revoke key).

Create src/app/api/v1/conversations/route.ts (GET - list conversations for authenticated client) and src/app/api/v1/conversations/[conversationId]/route.ts (GET - conversation detail with turns and scores).

Write comprehensive tests in tests/: tests/lib/api-keys.test.ts (generation, hashing, validation), tests/api/ingest.test.ts (valid ingestion, invalid payloads, missing/invalid API key, rate limiting), tests/lib/rbac.test.ts (role enforcement), tests/lib/tenant.test.ts (data isolation - one client cannot access another's data). Use Jest with mocked Prisma client and mocked BullMQ.
Add npm scripts to package.json: dev, build, start, lint, typecheck (tsc --noEmit), test (jest), test:watch, db:generate (prisma generate), db:migrate (prisma migrate dev), db:push (prisma db push).
acceptance_criteria: npm run typecheck passes with zero errors
npm test passes all tests in tests/lib/api-keys.test.ts, tests/api/ingest.test.ts, tests/lib/rbac.test.ts, tests/lib/tenant.test.ts
Prisma schema includes all entities listed with proper relations and indexes
Ingestion endpoint validates input with Zod and returns appropriate error responses for malformed requests
API key authentication rejects requests without valid keys
RBAC tests confirm Admin can access all routes, Reviewer has limited access
Data isolation tests confirm cross-tenant access is impossible
findings: All verification steps pass. Had to install ts-node as additional dev dependency for Jest TS config. Fixed BullMQ type incompatibility by using ConnectionOptions instead of direct IORedis instance. Prisma JSON fields require explicit cast with Prisma.InputJsonValue. 51 tests passing across 4 test suites.
